controls.name: Baseline race (the 'free transcript' test)
controls.evidence: Pooled 26059 per-second observations, 263 positive (non-harness ≥5 hp loss or death within 60 s). AUC: T=0.561, hp alone=0.498, log rows/min (verbosity)=0.299. Legs NOT RUNNABLE: hostile count and time of day — no such series exists in the recorded stores. T beats every available baseline. RIDER: winning this race is a weak claim — AUC(T) sits far below C8's 0.75 absolute bar (see C8), the verbosity baseline is anti-predictive rather than competitive, and the hp inputs/labels for days 1–5 rest on the mis-scaled trace hp field (filing §2). C8 is the operative test.

Pooled harness share=0.6% — but the study's bar is per-day ("≤20% for a day to be used for pacing"), and day 9 fails it at 98.2%: on the retro-run the gate does exactly its job, certifying days 1–5 and 10 and refusing day 9, whose entire tension integral sits on harness-tagged ticks (its peaks are the crew's own death window — study failure mode 2, confirmed empirically). Day 10's top-decile membership is a tie artefact (510 rows tie at T=0). Harness-tagged ticks = FEED/RESPAWN mask windows from the traces + day 9's record-tagged harness death window (19:14:12–19:23:52Z, ±30 s).
